pamphlet_excerpts: Citizenship in The Community Means: Public policy includes the goals the government sets as well as the actions required to achieve those goals (p. 10).
Citizenship in The Community Means Principle 2: Some citizens do not vote, voluntarily giving up their voice in the government (p. 10).

Citizenship in The Community Means Principle 3: Other citizens do not know or care about what is going on in their community, until a prison is built in their neighborhood, orthe crime rate grows (p. 10).
Citizenship in The Community Means Principle 4: Unless they are upset about a particular issue, most citizens leave the decisions to elected representatives and local activists (p. 10).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Citizenship in The Community Means): People who feel connected to their community tend to participate (p. 10).
Step 2 (Citizenship in The Community Means): The more active citizens are in their community, with ties to a school, youth groups, businesses, and service clubs, the more interest they (p. 10).
Step 3 (Citizenship in The Community Means): That is why longtime residents often hold local offices (p. 10).
Step 4 (Citizenship in The Community Means): You have a chance now to build connections in your own community (p. 10).

quiz_item.question: In Citizenship in the Community Requirement 1, what distinguishes mandatory legal duties of a citizen from voluntary civic responsibilities that strengthen a local town or neighborhood?
options: A. Paying local taxes and obeying laws are optional suggestions, whereas running for mayor is legally required of every resident at age eighteen.
B. Serving on a jury when summoned is voluntary, whereas attending every weekly city council meeting is enforced by fine.

C. Obeying laws, paying taxes, and serving on a jury when summoned are legal duties, while staying informed on local issues, voting in municipal elections, and volunteering for community service are essential civic responsibilities.
D. Good citizenship requires avoiding all interaction with school boards, county commissioners, or neighborhood improvement groups.
